reason: The text features multiple regular human characters demonstrating agency throughout the narrative. Moses exhibits significant agency by: questioning God's plan (expressing doubt about the people's belief), objecting to the mission ('please send someone else'), and taking concrete actions (gathering his family and possessions to return to Egypt). Aaron demonstrates agency by choosing to go meet Moses and actively performing the signs before the people. The Israelite elders and people show agency through their deliberate choice to believe (וַֽיַּאֲמֵ֖ן הָעָ֑ם) and listen, and their responsive worship (וַֽיִּקְּד֖וּ וַיִּֽשְׁתַּחֲוּֽוּ). While God initiates events and provides direction, the human characters consistently make choices, raise objections, take actions, and respond with their own will.
story: Moses meets Yahweh in the Burning Bush
